title: P3: Coordination Simulation Harness
Design and implement SimContext in gossip-contracts
description:
Design and implement SimContext — the deterministic execution context for simulation testing of the coordination subsystem.

## Context

SimContext is the gateway to the entire simulation testing chain: it unblocks gossip-al3 (simulation harness), which unblocks gossip-0ee (proptest state machine tests). The dependency on gossip-irq (64-bit ID infrastructure) is now closed.

## What SimContext Provides

SimContext fills the one missing "pillar of determinism" in the coordination subsystem. The existing CoordinationBackend trait already satisfies 3 of 4 pillars:
- Abstract I/O: synchronous API, no I/O (D2.13)
- Single-threaded: &mut self enforces it
- Simulated clock: now: LogicalTime parameter on every method (D2.17)
- **MISSING**: Seeded PRNG — SimContext fills this gap

SimContext bundles a seeded PRNG (ChaCha8Rng), a simulated logical clock (LogicalTime), and the original seed for reproduction. It is the foundation for all randomized simulation operations (worker selection, fault injection timing, operation generation).

## Critical Research Findings (7 findings from 5-agent deep research)

### Finding 1: Reference code has 5 compilation-breaking bugs (CERTAIN)

The reference sim_context.rs in tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/dst_reference_code/ cannot compile against the actual codebase:

| # | Reference Code | Actual API | Required Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LogicalTime(10) | Private field — LogicalTime is a newtype with private inner | Use LogicalTime::from_raw(10) |
| 2 | self.clock.advance(ticks) | Method does not exist on LogicalTime | Use checked_add(u64) -> Option<LogicalTime>, then .expect() |
| 3 | FenceEpoch(0), ShardId(1), etc. | All have private fields | Use from_raw() constructors throughout |
| 4 | rand::rngs::StdRng | rand is not a dependency; StdRng is non-portable across Rust versions | Use rand_chacha::ChaCha8Rng (see Finding 2) |
| 5 | debug_assert! for time monotonicity in set_time() | Elided in release-mode simulation builds — time regression would silently corrupt state | Use assert! (always-on) for safety-critical invariants |

### Finding 2: ChaCha8Rng is the only safe PRNG choice (STRONG CONSENSUS — 4/5 agents)

StdRng is explicitly documented as non-portable: "The algorithm is unspecified and may change in any version" (rand docs). SmallRng is platform-dependent. ChaCha8Rng from rand_chacha is "deterministic and portable, tested against reference vectors" at 2.2 GB/s throughput. This is the standard choice for deterministic simulation (FoundationDB, TigerBeetle, sled all use fixed-algorithm PRNGs).

Sources: rand docs (https://docs.rs/rand/latest/rand/rngs/struct.StdRng.html), rand_chacha docs (https://docs.rs/rand_chacha/latest/rand_chacha/), corroborated by 4 of 5 research agents.

### Finding 3: Existing codebase is 75% simulation-ready

The CoordinationBackend trait already provides 3 of 4 determinism pillars. SimContext only needs to provide the seeded PRNG. No architectural changes needed to the existing coordination code.

### Finding 4: Highest-value faults are mundane (Yuan et al. OSDI 2014)

92% of catastrophic distributed system failures are in error-handling code. The highest-value test scenarios are: lease expiry, stale fences, op-log eviction — all already modeled in the existing error types (AcquireError::AlreadyLeased, RenewError::StaleFence, etc.).

### Finding 5: Two-phase simulation should be designed in (TigerBeetle evidence)

Safety Phase (faults on) then Liveness Phase (faults off, verify convergence). TigerBeetle found critical deadlocks only in liveness mode. 3/5 research agents recommend building two-phase support from the start. The harness should support run_two_phase(safety_ops, liveness_ops).

### Finding 6: Invariant checker covers only 10 of 14 spec invariants

ShardRecord::assert_invariants() checks 10 per-record structural invariants (INV-1 through INV-10). Missing 4 cross-record/temporal properties that require a simulator-level checker:
- INV-S01: Mutual exclusion — no two workers hold the same shard simultaneously
- INV-S02: Fence monotonicity — fence epoch never decreases across simulation steps
- INV-S05: Cursor monotonicity — cursor never regresses within a lease epoch
- INV-S06: Terminal irreversibility — once Done/Split/Parked, status never changes back

Additional invariants deferred to later (require tracking full operation history):
- INV-S09: Split coverage correctness
- INV-S11: Idempotency correctness
- INV-S13: Cursor bounds

### Finding 7: HashMap iteration is a latent risk

InMemoryCoordinator uses HashMap<(TenantId, ShardKey), ShardRecord>. Currently safe because only point lookups are used. Becomes a non-determinism risk when claim_next_available or any iteration-dependent operation is added. Document this; switch to BTreeMap before adding iteration-dependent ops.

## Implementation Plan (10 steps)

### Step 1: Add rand/rand_chacha as optional deps [S]
- Files: crates/gossip-contracts/Cargo.toml (workspace Cargo.toml if needed)
- Update test-support feature: test-support = ["dep:rand", "dep:rand_chacha"]
- Add as dev-dependencies too for tests (so #[cfg(test)] code can use them without the feature)
- Verify: cargo check --features test-support compiles; cargo check (no feature) does not pull them in

### Step 2: Create SimContext with ChaCha8Rng [M]
- File: crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/mod.rs (new)
- Struct: SimContext { rng: ChaCha8Rng, clock: LogicalTime, seed: u64 }
- Methods:
  - new(seed: u64) -> Self — seeds ChaCha8Rng via SeedableRng::seed_from_u64, clock starts at LogicalTime::ZERO
  - now(&self) -> LogicalTime
  - advance(&mut self, ticks: u64) — uses clock.checked_add(ticks).expect("SimContext clock overflow")
  - set_time(&mut self, time: LogicalTime) — uses assert!(time >= self.clock) NOT debug_assert!
  - rng(&mut self) -> &mut ChaCha8Rng
  - seed(&self) -> u64
- Wire up in lib.rs: #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))] pub mod sim;
- Evidence: F1 (API fixes), F2 (ChaCha8Rng), F5 (assert! not debug_assert!)

### Step 3: Create FaultLevel and FaultConfig [S]
- File: crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/mod.rs (same file as SimContext)
- FaultLevel enum: SunnyDay = 1, Stormy = 2, Radioactive = 3
  - Derive: Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash
- FaultConfig struct with fields:
  - drop_rate: f64 (0.0 = none, 1.0 = all)
  - max_delay: u64 (max message delay in logical ticks)
  - inject_pauses: bool
  - pause_range: (u64, u64) — [min, max] tick range
  - inject_lease_expiry: bool
  - inject_storage_corruption: bool
- FaultConfig::for_level(level: FaultLevel) -> Self:
  - SunnyDay: all defaults (no faults)
  - Stormy: drop_rate=0.1, max_delay=50, pauses on (10-100), lease_expiry on, NO storage corruption
  - Radioactive: drop_rate=0.3, max_delay=200, pauses on (10-500), lease_expiry on, storage corruption ON
- FaultConfig is separate from SimContext (consensus from research)

### Step 4: Build SimWorker [S]
- File: crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/worker.rs (new)
- SimWorker struct:
  - id: WorkerId
  - held_shards: Vec<(ShardKey, FenceEpoch)> — uses ShardKey not bare ShardId (matches InMemoryCoordinator keying)
  - next_op: u64 — monotonic counter for generating unique OpId values
  - paused: bool — for fault injection (simulated process pause)
- Methods:
  - new(id: WorkerId) -> Self
  - gen_op_id(&mut self) -> OpId — uses next_op counter, increments
  - acquire_shard(&mut self, key: ShardKey, fence: FenceEpoch)
  - release_shard(&mut self, key: &ShardKey)
  - holds_shard(&self, key: &ShardKey) -> bool
  - is_paused(&self) -> bool
  - pause(&mut self) / resume(&mut self)
- Uses from_raw() constructors throughout

### Step 5: Build InvariantChecker [M]
- File: crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/invariants.rs (new)
- Uses BTreeMap (not HashMap) for its own state — deterministic iteration
- Tracks:
  - shard_owners: BTreeMap<ShardKey, WorkerId> — who holds what
  - fence_high_water: BTreeMap<ShardKey, FenceEpoch> — highest fence seen per shard
  - terminal_shards: BTreeSet<ShardKey> — shards that reached terminal state
  - cursor_at_fence: BTreeMap<(ShardKey, FenceEpoch), Vec<u8>> — last cursor per (shard, epoch) for monotonicity
- Methods:
  - new() -> Self
  - check_acquire(&mut self, key: ShardKey, worker: WorkerId, fence: FenceEpoch) — updates shard_owners, checks fence monotonicity
  - check_release(&mut self, key: &ShardKey) — removes from shard_owners
  - check_terminal(&mut self, key: ShardKey) — adds to terminal_shards
  - check_cursor(&mut self, key: ShardKey, fence: FenceEpoch, cursor: &[u8]) — checks monotonicity within epoch
  - check_mutual_exclusion(&self) — verify no shard has two owners (should be structurally impossible but belt-and-suspenders)
  - violations(&self) -> &[InvariantViolation] — collected violations instead of panicking (allows reporting)
- InvariantViolation enum:
  - FenceRegression { key, old, new }
  - CursorRegression { key, fence, old_cursor, new_cursor }
  - TerminalMutation { key, operation }
  - MutualExclusionViolation { key, workers }
- Evidence: F6 (10/14 invariants), TigerBeetle VOPR pattern

### Step 6: Build CoordinationSim harness [L]
- File: crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/harness.rs (new)
- Drives the REAL InMemoryCoordinator (not a simplified SimBackend) — FoundationDB principle: test real code
- CoordinationSim struct:
  - ctx: SimContext
  - coordinator: InMemoryCoordinator
  - workers: Vec<SimWorker>
  - fault_config: FaultConfig
  - checker: InvariantChecker
  - trace: Vec<SimEvent> — operation log for debugging
  - tenant: TenantId — single tenant for now (multi-tenant deferred)
  - run: RunId
  - step_count: u64
- SimOp enum (operations the simulator can execute):
  - Acquire { worker_idx: usize, shard_key: ShardKey }
  - Checkpoint { worker_idx: usize, shard_key: ShardKey, cursor_key: Vec<u8> }
  - Complete { worker_idx: usize, shard_key: ShardKey, cursor_key: Vec<u8> }
  - Park { worker_idx: usize, shard_key: ShardKey, reason: ParkReason }
  - Renew { worker_idx: usize, shard_key: ShardKey }
  - SplitReplace { worker_idx: usize, shard_key: ShardKey, children: Vec<SplitReplaceChild> }
  - SplitResidual { worker_idx: usize, shard_key: ShardKey, split_point: Vec<u8> }
  - AdvanceTime { ticks: u64 }
  - PauseWorker { worker_idx: usize }
  - ResumeWorker { worker_idx: usize }
- SimEvent struct: { step: u64, op: SimOp, result: SimOpResult } for trace
- Key methods:
  - new(seed: u64, num_workers: usize, num_shards: usize, fault_config: FaultConfig) -> Self
  - step(&mut self, op: SimOp) -> SimOpResult — execute op on real coordinator, run invariant checks, record trace
  - run_random(&mut self, n: usize) — generate and execute n random ops using ctx.rng()
  - run_two_phase(&mut self, safety_ops: usize, liveness_ops: usize) — safety phase with faults, then liveness phase with SunnyDay config
  - report(&self) -> SimReport — summary of violations, step count, seed
- SimReport struct: { seed: u64, steps: u64, violations: Vec<InvariantViolation>, trace_len: usize }

design:
## Architectural Decisions

### AD-1: ChaCha8Rng, not StdRng (LOCKED)
StdRng documentation explicitly states: "The algorithm is unspecified and may change in any version." Using StdRng means a Rust toolchain update silently breaks every stored seed and reproduction path. ChaCha8Rng from rand_chacha is portable across platforms and Rust versions, tested against reference vectors, and runs at 2.2 GB/s. This is non-negotiable.
- Evidence: rand docs, rand_chacha docs, 4/5 research agents concur

### AD-2: assert! not debug_assert! for monotonicity (LOCKED)
The reference code uses debug_assert! for time monotonicity in set_time(). This is elided in release builds. Since simulation harnesses may run in release mode for performance, a time regression would silently corrupt state. Use assert! for all safety-critical invariants in simulation code.
- Evidence: Finding 1 bug 5, TigerBeetle Tiger Style philosophy

### AD-3: FaultConfig separate from SimContext (CONSENSUS)
SimContext owns the PRNG and clock. FaultConfig is a configuration knob passed to the harness. Keeping them separate allows the same SimContext to run under different fault regimes and avoids coupling randomness source with fault policy.
- Evidence: 3/5 research agents, FoundationDB pattern

### AD-4: Drive real InMemoryCoordinator, not a mock (LOCKED)
The simulation harness must exercise the actual InMemoryCoordinator implementation. Creating a simplified "SimBackend" would test a different code path than production. FoundationDB's core insight: simulate real code with fake I/O, don't simulate fake code.
- Evidence: FoundationDB SIGMOD 2021, consensus across all 5 agents

### AD-5: Two-phase simulation from day one (RECOMMENDED)
Safety Phase (inject faults, verify no invariant violations) then Liveness Phase (stop faults, verify convergence to stable state). TigerBeetle found critical deadlocks only in liveness mode. Building two-phase support later requires retrofitting the harness.
- Evidence: TigerBeetle VOPR, 3/5 research agents

### AD-6: BTreeMap in InvariantChecker (LOCKED)
The InvariantChecker must use BTreeMap/BTreeSet for all its internal state to guarantee deterministic iteration order. HashMap iteration order varies between runs (randomized hashing), which would make invariant checking non-deterministic.

### AD-7: ShardKey not bare ShardId in SimWorker (LOCKED)
InMemoryCoordinator keys by (TenantId, ShardKey) where ShardKey = (RunId, ShardId). SimWorker must track held_shards as Vec<(ShardKey, FenceEpoch)> to match the coordinator's keying, not bare ShardId.

### AD-8: Collect violations, don't panic (RECOMMENDED)
The InvariantChecker should collect InvariantViolation values rather than panicking on first violation. This enables:
- Complete violation reports (all problems, not just the first)
- Deterministic replay comparison (compare violation sets)
- Test assertions on expected violation counts

## Reference Code API Mapping

Every place the reference sim_context.rs uses a constructor must be mapped to the actual API:

| Type | Reference | Actual | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| LogicalTime | LogicalTime(n) | LogicalTime::from_raw(n) | Private field |
| LogicalTime | clock.advance(ticks) | clock.checked_add(ticks).expect("overflow") | Returns Option, no advance method |
| FenceEpoch | FenceEpoch(0) | FenceEpoch::ZERO or FenceEpoch::from_raw(0) | Private field |
| FenceEpoch | FenceEpoch(1) | FenceEpoch::INITIAL or FenceEpoch::from_raw(1) | Private field |
| ShardId | ShardId(n) | ShardId::from_raw(n) | Private field |
| WorkerId | WorkerId(n) | WorkerId::from_raw(n) | Private field |
| RunId | RunId(n) | RunId::from_raw(n) | Private field |
| OpId | OpId(n) | OpId::from_raw(n) | Private field |
| TenantId | TenantId([..]) | TenantId::from_bytes([u8; 32]) | 32-byte array |
| ShardKey | (RunId, ShardId) | ShardKey::new(RunId, ShardId) | Compound type |
| Lease | Lease::new(..) | Lease::new(..) | pub(crate) — accessible from sim module inside crate |
| ShardRecord | ShardRecord::new_active(..) | ShardRecord::new_active(..) | pub(crate) — accessible from sim module |
| PRNG | rand::rngs::StdRng | rand_chacha::ChaCha8Rng | Different crate |

## Invariant Coverage Map

### Covered by ShardRecord::assert_invariants() (10 invariants):
- INV-1: park_reason.is_some() iff status == Parked
- INV-2: Structural (Option<LeaseHolder>)
- INV-3: Terminal shards have no lease
- INV-4: fence_epoch >= INITIAL
- INV-5: op_log.len() <= OP_LOG_CAP (16)
- INV-6: Split implies spawned non-empty
- INV-7: parent.is_some() implies shard.is_derived()
- INV-7b: is_derived() implies parent.is_some()
- INV-8: All spawned entries are derived
- INV-9: Op-log entries have unique OpId values
- INV-10: spawned.len() <= MAX_SPAWNED_PER_SHARD (1024)

### Must be covered by InvariantChecker (4 cross-record invariants):
- INV-S01: Mutual exclusion — no two workers hold the same shard at the same time
- INV-S02: Fence monotonicity — fence epoch never decreases across simulation steps
- INV-S05: Cursor monotonicity — cursor.last_key never regresses within a lease epoch
- INV-S06: Terminal irreversibility — once Done/Split/Parked, status never changes back

### Deferred (require full operation history tracking):
- INV-S09: Split coverage — children exactly partition parent range
- INV-S11: Idempotency — same (op_id, payload_hash) returns cached result
- INV-S13: Cursor bounds — cursor.last_key within [spec.start, spec.end)

## HashMap Non-Determinism Risk Assessment

InMemoryCoordinator uses HashMap<(TenantId, ShardKey), ShardRecord>. Current operations are ALL point lookups (get/get_mut/insert/remove by exact key), which are deterministic regardless of HashMap iteration order.

Risk activates when iteration-dependent operations are added:
- claim_next_available (scan all shards, pick one)
- list_shards (return ordered list)
- any operation that iterates over the map

Mitigation: Document in the coordinator that HashMap iteration must never be relied upon for ordering. When claim_next_available is implemented, switch to BTreeMap or add a deterministic secondary index.

title: Replace hand-rolled binary search with partition_point
description:
## Context
The InMemoryDeterministicConnector contains 24 lines of hand-rolled binary search across lower_bound and upper_bound functions. These are functionally equivalent to slice::partition_point from std.

## Current State
crates/gossip-connectors/src/in_memory.rs lines 387-417: two 12-line functions with manual loop mechanics.

## Desired State
Replace with one-liner std equivalents:
```rust
fn lower_bound(items: &[MemItem], key: &[u8]) -> usize {
    items.partition_point(|item| item.key.as_bytes() < key)
}
fn upper_bound(items: &[MemItem], key: &[u8]) -> usize {
    items.partition_point(|item| item.key.as_bytes() <= key)
}
```
The < vs <= distinction remains equally visible.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Add coordination protocol fuzz target
description:
## Coordination protocol fuzz target

### Problem
Fuzz targets exist for identity types (fuzz_item_key, fuzz_derivation_chain) and ring buffer (fuzz_ring_buffer) but NOT for the coordination protocol. The coordination protocol's operation sequences under simulation are explored via proptest (random strategies with shrinking) but NOT via coverage-guided mutation (cargo-fuzz/libfuzzer).

### Research Basis

**P1.4.F5 (arbitrary Crate for Structured Fuzzing, Evidence 4):** The arbitrary crate transforms raw fuzzer bytes into structured Rust types via #[derive(Arbitrary)]. For coordination fuzzing, libfuzzer's feedback loop learns which byte patterns produce interesting coordinator states. Fuzzing finds crash/panic paths via coverage-guided mutation; proptest finds property violations via random exploration with shrinking. They are complementary and find different bug classes. Source: https://github.com/rust-fuzz/arbitrary, https://docs.rs/arbitrary/

**P1.5.F9 (Mallory Framework, Evidence 3):** Grey-box fuzzing using timeline feedback finds bugs more effectively than black-box approaches. Found 22 zero-day bugs in distributed systems (Braft, Dqlite, Redis). Source: arxiv.org/abs/2305.02601

### Implementation

Create crates/gossip-contracts/fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_coordination.rs:

1. Define FuzzOp enum with #[derive(Arbitrary)]:
   - Acquire { worker: u8, shard: u8 }
   - Renew { worker: u8, shard: u8 }
   - Checkpoint { worker: u8, shard: u8, cursor_byte: u8 }
   - Complete { worker: u8, shard: u8, cursor_byte: u8 }
   - Park { worker: u8, shard: u8 }
   - SplitReplace { worker: u8, shard: u8, mid_byte: u8 }
   - AdvanceTime { ticks: u8 }

2. Map FuzzOp to SimOp:
   - Clamp worker to 1..=4, shard to 1..=8
   - Convert u8 fields to proper types (WorkerId, ShardId, etc.)

3. Fuzz target body:
   - Parse input bytes into Vec<FuzzOp> via Arbitrary
   - Create CoordinationSim::new(0, FaultLevel::SunnyDay).with_workers_and_shards(4, 8)
   - For each FuzzOp: map to SimOp, call sim.step(), assert violations.is_empty()
   - Panic on any invariant violation (libfuzzer treats panics as findings)

4. Add to Cargo.toml [[bin]] section (follow existing fuzz target pattern).

### Key Code References
- fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_item_key.rs — existing fuzz target pattern
- fuzz/Cargo.toml — fuzz target registration
- harness.rs:101-141 — SimOp enum (map FuzzOp variants to these)
- harness.rs:646-653 — step() method (execute op + check invariants)
- harness.rs:544-557 — CoordinationSim::new() constructor

### Verification
cargo +nightly fuzz run fuzz_coordination -- -max_total_time=60

### Reading
- arbitrary crate docs (docs.rs/arbitrary/) — structured fuzz input
- cargo-fuzz book (rust-fuzz.github.io/book/) — Rust fuzzing guide
- Mallory paper (arxiv.org/abs/2305.02601) — grey-box fuzz testing of distributed systems

Remove per-query allocations from claim/list coordinator paths
description:
## Context
Claim/list query flows still allocate per request in production. This keeps allocator pressure on a core scheduling path (`default_claim_next_available` + `list_shards`) and violates the no-allocation-after-startup objective.

## Current State
`list_shards` materializes a `Vec<ShardSummary>`, and `ShardSummary` currently owns copied key bytes.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:2344
let mut summaries = Vec::with_capacity(shard_ids.map_or(0, |ids| ids.len()));
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:2361-2362
let summary = ShardSummary::from_record(record, now, &self.slab);
summaries.push(summary);
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/run.rs:1368-1370
last_key: record.cursor.last_key(slab).map(|k| k.into()),
key_range_start: record.spec.key_range_start(slab).into(),
key_range_end: record.spec.key_range_end(slab).into(),
```

`facade::default_claim_next_available` also triggers repeated `list_shards` materialization calls.

## Desired State
Claim/list code paths use borrowed views or caller-provided reusable output buffers so repeated query traffic does not allocate after startup. Selection logic should avoid owned `ShardSummary` allocations in steady state.

## Implementation Guidance
### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs | Add allocation-free list/query API variant (`list_shards_into` or borrowed iterator/view) | Eliminate per-query `Vec` growth/materialization |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/run.rs | Introduce borrowed summary/view type to avoid key byte cloning | Remove owned hot-path copies |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/facade.rs | Route `default_claim_next_available` through allocation-free list path | Keep claim path allocator-closed |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/traits.rs | Extend trait contract for scratch/output-buffer based list operations | Preserve backend abstraction |

### Patterns to Follow
Mirror `acquire_and_restore_into` + `AcquireScratch` ownership pattern for list/query APIs to keep buffers outside per-call backend allocation.

### Utilities to Reuse
- Existing `ShardFilter::matches_record` pre-filtering (already avoids some wasted summary creation)
- Existing slab-backed accessors on `ShardRecord` for borrowed byte slices

### Blast Radius
- `default_claim_next_available`
- Any callers consuming `Vec<ShardSummary>` directly
- Run-progress/reporting APIs that currently rely on owned summaries

## Code References
```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/facade.rs:239-241
let summaries = backend
    .list_shards(now, tenant, run, ShardFilter::available())
    .map_err(ClaimError::from)?;
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/facade.rs:248-252
.list_shards(now, tenant, run, ShardFilter::active())
.unwrap_or_default()
.iter()
.filter_map(|s| s.lease_deadline())
.min();
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:2366-2370
summaries.sort_by(|a, b| {
    a.key_range_start()
        .cmp(b.key_range_start())
        .then_with(|| a.shard().cmp(&b.shard()))
});
```

## Design Notes
Two valid approaches exist:
1. Borrowed summary view iterators over run_shards index.
2. Caller-owned output buffer (`&mut Vec<_>`/scratch) that is reused across calls.
Choose one primary API and keep legacy owned API as compatibility wrapper.

## Performance Considerations
This is a frequent control-plane path. Removing per-call allocations should materially reduce allocator contention under many-worker claim loops.

## Testing Strategy
- Add allocation-guard tests for repeated `default_claim_next_available` and `list_shards` loops after warmup.
- Preserve ordering/filter semantics with deterministic comparison tests between old owned API and new allocation-free API.

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-oi59 | Tier-2: Remove acquire/snapshot allocations after startup | relates-to |
| gossip-cpau | Eliminate heap materialization on checkpoint/complete validation hot paths | relates-to (closed) |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Claim/list steady-state path executes with zero post-warmup allocations.
- [ ] Output ordering/filter semantics remain unchanged.
- [ ] Compatibility behavior for existing `list_shards` consumers is preserved.
- [ ] Allocation regression tests cover both available and active shard query modes.
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test`.
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
- [ ] Docs build clean: `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`.

## Pointers
- Audit anchors: `in_memory.rs:2344`, `2361`, `2362`; `run.rs:1368-1370`; `facade.rs:239`, `248`.
- Keep idempotency and tenant isolation semantics unchanged while refactoring query API surface.

Eliminate post-startup coordinator map/set growth allocations
description:
## Context
The coordinator still performs post-startup allocations when hash maps/sets grow beyond conservative initial capacities. This violates the runtime contract that production hot paths must run allocation-free after startup warmup.

## Current State
`InMemoryCoordinator` pre-sizes several maps with small constants and then grows them dynamically through `entry`/`insert` paths.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:122-129
const TOP_LEVEL_SHARDS_MAP_MIN_INITIAL_CAPACITY: usize = 4;
const TOP_LEVEL_SHARDS_MAP_MAX_INITIAL_CAPACITY: usize = 16;
const TOP_LEVEL_RUNS_MAP_INITIAL_CAPACITY: usize = 8;
const TOP_LEVEL_RUN_SHARDS_MAP_INITIAL_CAPACITY: usize = 8;
const TOP_LEVEL_CLAIM_COOLDOWNS_MAP_INITIAL_CAPACITY: usize = 8;
const TENANT_SHARDS_MAP_MIN_INITIAL_CAPACITY: usize = 4;
const TENANT_SHARDS_MAP_MAX_INITIAL_CAPACITY: usize = 32;
const RUN_SHARD_SET_INITIAL_CAPACITY: usize = 8;
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:607-615
shards: ahash_map_with_capacity(top_level_shards_capacity),
runs: ahash_map_with_capacity(TOP_LEVEL_RUNS_MAP_INITIAL_CAPACITY),
run_shards: ahash_map_with_capacity(TOP_LEVEL_RUN_SHARDS_MAP_INITIAL_CAPACITY),
claim_cooldowns: ahash_map_with_capacity(
    TOP_LEVEL_CLAIM_COOLDOWNS_MAP_INITIAL_CAPACITY,
),
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:791-793
self.shards
    .entry(tenant)
    .or_insert_with(|| ahash_map_with_capacity(inner_initial_capacity));
```

`index_shard` and cooldown updates also insert into structures that may rehash after startup.

## Desired State
Coordinator map/set capacities are fully budgeted before serving runtime traffic, and mutation paths do not trigger allocator activity after startup. If runtime would exceed configured budgets, operations fail with explicit capacity/resource errors instead of growing containers.

## Implementation Guidance
### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs | Add fixed-capacity/pre-reserved map-set budgeting and growth guards for top-level and tenant-level structures | Remove runtime rehash/growth allocations |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/error.rs | Add/extend capacity error variants for map growth denial | Preserve deterministic failure behavior when budgets are exceeded |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory_tests.rs (or nearest test module) | Add allocation-regression tests for repeated insert/index/claim traffic after warmup | Prevent allocator regressions |

### Patterns to Follow
Use existing constructor-time capacity derivation patterns (`top_level_shards_map_initial_capacity` and `ahash_*_with_capacity`) and extend them into explicit no-growth runtime invariants.

### Utilities to Reuse
- `ahash_map_with_capacity` and `ahash_set_with_capacity` helpers
- Existing shard limit checks (`check_shard_limits`) as the model for fail-fast capacity enforcement

### Blast Radius
- `shard_insert` tenant-map creation
- `index_shard` run->shard set insertion
- `register_shards` run set extension
- `record_claim` cooldown map insertion
- Any call sites relying on implicit growth behavior

## Code References
```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:1914-1917
self.run_shards
    .entry((tenant, run))
    .or_insert_with(|| ahash_set_with_capacity(RUN_SHARD_SET_INITIAL_CAPACITY))
    .insert(shard);
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:2241-2243
.entry((tenant, run))
.or_insert_with(|| ahash_set_with_capacity(shard_ids.len()))
.extend(shard_ids.iter().copied());
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:2708
self.claim_cooldowns.insert(worker, now);
```

## Performance Considerations
These are hot coordinator paths. Replace amortized-growth assumptions with deterministic capacity accounting so steady-state runtime avoids allocator interaction entirely.

## Testing Strategy
- Add a deterministic allocation-guard test that warms coordinator state, then executes large steady-state operation loops (`shard_insert`/`index_shard`/claim cooldown updates) and asserts zero post-warmup allocations.
- Add a boundary test that exceeds configured map/set budgets and expects typed capacity errors (not panics).

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-oi59 | Tier-2: Remove acquire/snapshot allocations after startup | relates-to |
| gossip-hk3y | Pre-size all coordinator HashMaps with with_capacity | relates-to (closed predecessor) |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Coordinator map/set mutation paths do not allocate after startup warmup under configured capacity budgets.
- [ ] Exceeding configured map/set budgets yields explicit recoverable errors.
- [ ] Allocation regression tests cover map growth-sensitive paths.
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test`.
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
- [ ] Docs build clean: `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`.

## Pointers
- Audit anchors: `in_memory.rs:122-129`, `607-614`, `792`, `1915`, `2241`, `2708`.
- Reuse existing shard limit guard style for deterministic capacity failures.

description:
## Context
`split_replace` and `split_residual` still allocate temporary vectors/sets in production operation paths. These operations are part of runtime shard lifecycle management and must be allocation-stable after startup.

## Current State
Split helpers create transient heap structures for sorting, validation, staging inserts, and replay probing.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:1444-1445
) -> Result<Vec<&'a SplitReplaceChild<'a>>, SplitReplaceError> {
    let sorted = split_replace_sort_children(plan);
```

```rust

let child_specs: Vec<ShardSpecRef<'_>> = sorted.iter().map(|c| c.spec()).collect();
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:1576
let mut to_insert: Vec<ShardMapEntry> = Vec::with_capacity(sorted.len());
```

Residual replay lookup also allocates a hash set per call.

## Desired State
Split operations use bounded inline/caller-owned scratch memory for sorting, validation, and replay detection so no heap allocation occurs once startup warmup completes.

## Implementation Guidance
### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs | Replace split helper temporary `Vec`/`HashSet` usage with inline/scratch buffers and allocation-free replay probe strategy | Remove runtime split allocations |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/split.rs (if needed) | Add bounded helper abstractions for split scratch | Centralize reusable split scratch semantics |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/*tests* | Add split-specific allocation guard tests (replace + residual) | Prevent regressions |

### Patterns to Follow
Use `InlineVec` for bounded fanout children and avoid `HashSet` materialization by scanning deterministic derived IDs directly against spawned lineage with bounded loops.

### Utilities to Reuse
- `InlineVec<ShardId, MAX_SPLIT_CHILDREN>` already used in split path
- `MAX_SPAWNED_PER_SHARD` bound to size fixed scratch buffers safely

### Blast Radius
- `split_replace_validate_preconditions`
- `split_replace_sort_children`
- `split_replace_build_children`
- `find_replayed_residual`
- `split_residual_apply_parent`

## Code References
```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:1488-1490
let mut sorted: Vec<&SplitReplaceChild<'a>> = plan.children().iter().collect();
sorted.sort_by(|a, b| a.spec().key_range_start().cmp(b.spec().key_range_start()));
```


## Design Notes
Two implementation strategies are acceptable:
1. Introduce a dedicated `SplitScratch` reusable structure and thread through split APIs.
2. Use fixed-size inline containers constrained by existing split bounds.
Prefer option (1) if it keeps code clearer while preserving no-allocation constraints.

## Performance Considerations
Split operations are less frequent than claim/checkpoint but can run under overload and should not trigger allocator bursts when many workers split concurrently.

## Testing Strategy
- Add stress tests for repeated split-replace/split-residual loops with allocation guard enabled post-warmup.
- Preserve replay/idempotency semantics under both op-log hit and spawned-lineage fallback paths.

## Related Work

description:
## Finding: Budgets::is_expired() calls Instant::now() internally — breaks deterministic simulation testing

**Severity**: SHOULD FIX
**File(s)**: crates/gossip-contracts/src/connector/types.rs:871-874
**Type**: design (DST incompatibility)
**Source**: PR #56 review

### Problem

`Budgets::is_expired()` calls `Instant::now()` internally, making it non-deterministic. The project uses `LogicalTime` (a u64 newtype) for all time-dependent coordination logic specifically to enable deterministic simulation testing (DST). The scan loop (T13/gossip-9u1j.13) takes a `now_fn` parameter to control the clock source. When `Budgets` is used in the scan loop, `is_expired()` will bypass the deterministic clock, making scan loop deadline behavior untestable in simulation.

Current code (types.rs:871-874):
```rust
pub fn is_expired(&self) -> bool {
    self.deadline
        .is_some_and(|deadline| Instant::now() >= deadline)
}
```

### Resolution Steps

1. Read surrounding code to understand existing patterns
2. Change `is_expired` signature from `is_expired(&self) -> bool` to `is_expired(&self, now: Instant) -> bool`
3. Update the method body to use the provided `now` instead of `Instant::now()`
4. Update the doc comment to document the `now` parameter
5. Update the `budgets_is_expired_respects_deadline` test (types.rs:1210-1230) to pass explicit Instant values. This also fixes a secondary issue where the test relied on monotonic clock granularity for a boundary assertion.
6. Run full suite: `cargo test -p gossip-contracts`
7. Verify clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `is_expired` accepts `now: Instant` parameter instead of calling `Instant::now()`
- [ ] Doc comment for `is_expired` documents the `now` parameter
- [ ] Test `budgets_is_expired_respects_deadline` passes with explicit Instant values (no timing sensitivity)
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test -p gossip-contracts`
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features` passes

description:
Port traits.rs and in_memory.rs (shard operations only). Fix bug S4 (split replay panic). Decompose long functions per Tiger Style. Add property test H1 (random op sequence — highest ROI test).

## Source artifacts
- tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b2_phase2_coordination_final_code/traits.rs
- tmp/gossip-project-artifacts/b2_phase2_coordination_final_code/in_memory.rs

## Target files
- crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/traits.rs
- crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs

## Bug fix S4 (safety — 4 agents flagged, data integrity review marked CRITICAL)
split_replace at in_memory.rs:387-390 panics on child ID collision: panic!("derived child shard id collision"). After op-log eviction (16+ subsequent ops), retrying the split hits this panic because the deterministic child IDs already exist but the op-log entry is gone. Fix with state-based replay detection:
  // In split_replace: if all derived children already exist AND parent is Split
  if self.shards.contains_key(&(tenant, child_key)) {
      // State-based replay: deterministic ID already exists
      // Verify parent status is Split and ALL children exist
      // Return Replayed(SplitReplaceResult { children })
  }
Similarly for split_residual: if residual shard already exists and parent spec was already shrunk, return Replayed.

## Tiger Style: decompose long functions (70-line limit)
- split_replace (~120 lines) -> validate_split_plan() + create_split_children() + finalize_split_parent()
- split_residual (~101 lines) -> validate_residual_plan() + create_residual_shard() + shrink_parent_spec()
- register_shards (~95 lines) -> validate_and_canonicalize_manifest() + create_initial_shards()

## Tiger Style: loop upper bounds
assert!(plan.children.len() <= MAX_SPLIT_CHILDREN, "split children exceed limit");
for (i, child) in ordered.iter().enumerate() { ... }

## Lease field visibility (architecture review)
Make Lease fields pub(crate) with getters. The lease is a capability token — callers should not be able to forge one by constructing with arbitrary fields.

## Events integration
Wire StateTransitionEvent emission markers at each mutation site. Currently the events module is designed but zero integration points exist. At minimum, add // TODO(events): emit ShardAcquired/Checkpointed/Completed/Parked/Split markers.

## seed_shard test helper
Add missing assert_invariants() call.

## Security hardening (SEC-2)
Add MAX_SPLIT_CHILDREN = 256 constant and assert before iterating SplitReplacePlan.children — prevents unbounded allocation from malicious input.

## Property tests to add
- P1 (highest ROI — test strategy review unanimous): Random operation sequence preserves all invariants. Use proptest with custom Strategy:
  enum Op { Acquire, Checkpoint, Complete, Park, SplitReplace, SplitResidual, Renew, TimeAdvance }
  Generate sequences of 100+ ops with 2-3 workers. Assert assert_invariants() after every operation. For longer sequences (10,000+ steps), use raw StdRng with seeded RNG (proptest shrinking is useless at that scale).
- P2: Fence monotonicity — arbitrary worker interleavings of acquire/release -> fence_epoch never decreases per shard
- Cursor monotonicity — any sequence of checkpoints -> cursor never regresses
- Op-log eviction edge cases: Push 17 entries, retry first (evicted). Verify treated as new, not panic.
- Split replay after eviction: Push 16+ ops after split, retry split. Verify Replayed, not panic.
- Fencing mutual exclusion: For any two workers with different fence epochs, at most one can commit.

## Research context for fencing implementation
- Hochstein's 2025 FizzBee model: resource must reject <= (not just <). B2's strict equality check (lease.fence != record.fence_epoch) is correct and stronger.
- Idempotency-before-fencing ordering in checkpoint() follows Stripe's pattern: replays succeed even after shard transitions.
- Fence epoch as sole ownership proof is correct per formal models. Add debug_assert!(lease.owner == record.lease_owner.unwrap()) in debug builds.
- Jepsen proved etcd's lease-only locking loses 18% of acknowledged updates. B2's dual-check (fence + lease deadline) addresses this.

## claim_next_available performance note (from performance review)
O(S log S) scan of all shards per run. Acceptable for in-memory backend but production backends need a secondary available-shards index. Add a doc comment noting this.

## op_log_push uses Vec::remove(0) (performance review)
O(n) memmove of 15 entries (~600 bytes). Should use VecDeque. However, at n=16 the absolute cost is negligible (~50ns). Keep Vec for now, add // PERF: consider VecDeque if OP_LOG_CAP increases comment.

## Acceptance criteria
- CoordinationBackend trait with 7 shard ops compiles
- InMemoryCoordinator implements all 7 ops
- Split replay after op-log eviction returns Replayed (not panic)
- No function exceeds 70 lines
- Property test P1 passes with 100+ ops x multiple workers
- All fencing edge cases tested
- cargo fmt && cargo check && cargo clippy clean

title: F3: Add message_digest field to EnumerateFailed variant
Add simulation overload scenarios with S8-S10 invariant predicates
description:
## Overview

Extend CoordinationSim with overload-specific SimOp variants, new invariant predicates S8-S10, and three-phase test runs (warmup/overload/recovery). Validates the credit piggybacking (gossip-tybv) and claim cooldown (gossip-mynu) under adversarial conditions.

## Research Evidence

### Why Simulation Is the Top Priority Testing Strategy

**P1.8.F1 (Testing gold standard, Evidence 5):** FoundationDB, TigerBeetle, and sled all converge on deterministic simulation: abstract all nondeterminism behind injectable interfaces, drive state machine with random ops, check invariants after every step. TigerBeetle VOPR compresses 39 minutes of real-world testing into 3.3 seconds.

**P4.4.F5 (AWS mandate):** AWS Builders' Library explicitly recommends continuous load testing 'beyond breaking points' before production deployment. The 'start simple' philosophy implicitly defers this validation.

**P3.4.F4 (Three-phase model):** Existing run() has two phases: safety + liveness. For overload testing, structure should be: (1) Warmup — establish baseline, (2) Overload ramp — inject stress, (3) Recovery — remove pressure, verify convergence. Maps to TigerBeetle VOPR: Sunny = no overload, Stormy = intermittent bursts, Radioactive = sustained overload.

**P1.6.F5 (Existing infrastructure):** gossip-rs already depends on proptest 1.10, has CoordinationSim with FaultConfig PPM rates, InvariantChecker S1-S7, and deterministic ChaCha8Rng seeding. Overload control invariants can be added as new InvariantChecker predicates requiring ZERO new infrastructure.

**P1.8.F7 (Tiger-style):** Overload control invariants as inline assertions: debug_assert!(tokens <= max_tokens), debug_assert!(queue.len() <= capacity). Zero cost in release, caught by external checker in simulation.

### What the Sim Must Test

**P1.3.F1 (Metastable failure):** Overload -> retries -> more overload loop. Sim must verify system exits this state.

**P1.3.F5 (Thundering herd):** Mass lease expiry -> re-acquisition storm. Sim must verify claim cooldown prevents amplification.

**P1.3.F6 (Goodput collapse):** Over-aggressive admission -> oscillation (admit-all/reject-all). Sim must verify goodput floor maintained.

**P1.3.F4 (AIMD oscillation):** Even though we're not using AIMD, sim must verify credit signals don't cause oscillation.

## Files to Modify

### New SimOp Variants

In crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/harness.rs:49-81, add to SimOp enum (already #[non_exhaustive]):

- BurstClaim { count: u16 } — N workers simultaneously call claim_next_available. Tests coordinator under concurrent claim load (P4.2.F8). Simulates the O(N*S) worst case.
- CapacityDrop { pause_count: u16 } — Pause N active workers simultaneously. Tests system behavior when capacity suddenly shrinks (node failures, GC pauses). Leases will expire, triggering re-acquisition pressure.
- BurstShards { run: RunId, count: u16 } — Register N new shards into a run via register_shards. Tests admission behavior when claim surface suddenly expands. Validates split-aware accounting (P3.3.F6).

### New SimEvent Variants

In crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/harness.rs:90+, add to SimEvent enum:

- BurstClaimResults { succeeded: u16, throttled: u16, none_available: u16 } — Aggregated results from BurstClaim
- CapacityDropped { paused: Vec<WorkerId> } — Which workers were paused
- BurstShardsRegistered { count: u16 } — How many shards were registered

### New Invariant Predicates

In crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/invariants.rs, add to InvariantViolation enum (already #[non_exhaustive]):

**S8: AvailableCountAccuracy**
- After every acquire_and_restore, verify available_count in AcquireResult matches ground truth
- Ground truth: iterate all shards for the run, count those that are Active AND (no lease OR expired lease)
- Tolerance: exact match (count computed post-operation should be precise for InMemoryCoordinator)
- Tracked state: none needed (computed fresh each check)

**S9: CooldownEnforcement**
- No worker successfully acquired a shard within min_claim_interval of its previous acquisition
- Tracked state: last_successful_claim: BTreeMap<WorkerId, LogicalTime>
- On each check_all, for each Active shard with a lease: if lease.owner has a previous claim time, verify now - prev >= min_claim_interval

**S10: RecoveryConvergence**
- After overload phase ends (no more BurstClaim/CapacityDrop ops for T_recovery ticks), verify:
  (a) At least 1 shard reaches Complete status (system is making progress)
  (b) Claim success rate > 0 (system is not permanently stalled)
- Tracked state: overload_ended_at: Option<LogicalTime>, recovery_window: u64
- This is a liveness check, not safety — only checked in the recovery phase

### InvariantChecker State Additions

In crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/invariants.rs:83-94, add to InvariantChecker struct:

- last_claim_by_worker: BTreeMap<WorkerId, LogicalTime> — for S9
- overload_ended_at: Option<LogicalTime> — for S10
- recovery_ticks: u64 — configurable recovery window

### FaultConfig Extensions

In crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/mod.rs:160-311, add to FaultConfig:

- burst_claim_ppm: u32 — probability of BurstClaim per step (PPM)
- burst_claim_range: (u16, u16) — min/max count for BurstClaim
- capacity_drop_ppm: u32 — probability of CapacityDrop per step
- capacity_drop_range: (u16, u16) — min/max workers to pause
- burst_shards_ppm: u32 — probability of BurstShards per step
- burst_shards_range: (u16, u16) — min/max shards to register

FaultLevel mapping:
- SunnyDay: all overload PPMs = 0
- Stormy: burst_claim=30_000 (3%), capacity_drop=20_000 (2%), burst_shards=20_000 (2%)
- Radioactive: burst_claim=80_000 (8%), capacity_drop=50_000 (5%), burst_shards=50_000 (5%)

### Three-Phase Run Model

In crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/harness.rs, add method:

pub fn run_with_overload(&mut self, warmup: usize, overload: usize, recovery: usize) -> SimReport

Phase 1 (warmup): Normal ops only (suppress overload SimOps). Establish baseline.
Phase 2 (overload): Enable overload SimOps at configured FaultLevel rates.
Phase 3 (recovery): Suppress overload SimOps. Set overload_ended_at. Run S10 convergence check.

### Pass Criteria

For all scenarios:
1. Zero S1-S7 violations (non-negotiable safety floor — existing invariants)
2. Zero S8 violations (available_count accuracy)
3. Zero S9 violations (cooldown enforcement)
4. S10 convergence within recovery_ticks (configurable, default 100)
5. Goodput >= 10%: at least 10% of shards reach Complete during overload phase
6. No panics (tiger-style assertions in ShardRecord::assert_invariants())

### New Test Functions

In crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory_tests.rs or crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/:

- test_overload_sunny: SunnyDay fault level, 3 workers, 10 shards, 200 steps. Baseline.
- test_overload_stormy: Stormy, 5 workers, 20 shards, 500 steps. Intermittent bursts.
- test_overload_radioactive: Radioactive, 5 workers, 20 shards, 500 steps. Sustained stress.
- proptest_overload: Parameterized (seed, fault_level, workers, shards, overload_duration, recovery_duration). 50 cases per config.
- test_overload_deterministic_replay: Pinned seed that previously found a violation, verify fix.

## Design Decisions

1. **SimOp is #[non_exhaustive]:** Already designed for extension. New variants don't break existing code.
2. **PPM-based fault injection:** Consistent with existing FaultConfig pattern. Deterministic — same seed produces same fault sequence.
3. **Three-phase, not two-phase:** Recovery testing is where systems actually fail (P3.2.F5). Two-phase (safety+liveness) misses the recovery-after-overload behavior.
4. **S8 validates Step 1 (credit piggybacking):** If available_count is wrong, workers make bad decisions.
5. **S9 validates Step 2 (claim cooldown):** If cooldown is bypassed, claim storms remain unmitigated.
6. **S10 validates overall system health:** If the system doesn't recover after overload ends, something is fundamentally broken.

## Dependencies

- Depends on gossip-tybv (credit piggybacking) for S8 validation
- Depends on gossip-mynu (claim cooldown) for S9 validation
- Can be partially built before dependencies (SimOp variants + FaultConfig + three-phase model) with S8/S9 deferred until deps land

## References

1. FoundationDB simulation (Zhou et al., SIGMOD 2021) — deterministic simulation methodology
2. TigerBeetle VOPR blog (2023) — three difficulty levels, seed reproduction
3. Marc Brooker, 'Simple Simulations for System Builders' (2022) — modeling overload behavior
4. Amazon Builders' Library — load testing beyond breaking points
5. Bronson et al., 'Metastable Failures in Distributed Systems,' OSDI 2021 — sustaining feedback loops
6. Cho et al., 'Breakwater,' OSDI 2020 — goodput collapse analysis
notes: DEEPENED PLAN REFINEMENTS (2026-02-20): (1) Original S8 (AvailableCountAccuracy) downgraded to D1 diagnostic — CapacityHint is fail-open advisory metadata, not safety-critical. Keep existing unit tests, do not add to InvariantChecker. (2) S9 (CooldownEnforcement) confirmed as safety invariant — implement as push model: harness calls checker.record_claim_success(worker, now) after ClaimOk events. BTreeMap<WorkerId, LogicalTime> tracking. Vacuously true when cooldown_interval==0. (3) Original S10 (RecoveryConvergence) reclassified as L1 bounded liveness — checked once at end of recovery phase in OverloadReport, NOT in InvariantChecker. (4) No new SimOp variants — overload scenarios compose existing ops as scripted sequences (BurstClaim=all workers ClaimNext, CapacityDrop=pause half+advance time, BurstShards=SplitReplace all held). (5) 10% goodput threshold derived: 2x safety margin above theoretical livelock floor for 15→25 shards. (6) New file sim/overload.rs for OverloadScenario, OverloadKind, OverloadReport, GoodputTracker.

title: F1: Delete empty assert_invariants() on CapacityHint
[Conditional] Monotonic overload FSM — only if sim demonstrates need
description:
## Overview

4-state per-coordinator FSM: Normal -> Degraded -> Shedding -> Recovering -> Normal. Monotonic restriction ordering with asymmetric hysteresis thresholds. Pre-admission filter that gates acquire_and_restore before touching ShardRecord.

CONDITIONAL: Only implement if gossip-j6n4 (sim overload scenarios) Radioactive scenarios show goodput < 10% with credit piggybacking + claim cooldown alone.

## Research Evidence

### Why a State Machine (not just thresholds)

**P3.2.F2 (Minimal state set):** Production systems (CockroachDB, FoundationDB, Netflix) converge on 3-4 states with hysteresis. Three states (omitting Recovering) forces a binary jump from Shedding to Normal which causes goodput collapse oscillation (Google SRE Ch. 21, Brooker retry analysis). The Recovering state provides graduated AIMD-like ramp-up.

**P3.2.F4 (Formal monotonic invariant):** Define total order: Normal(0) < Recovering(1) < Degraded(2) < Shedding(3). Monotonic fallback: state can only increase restriction unless cooldown guard satisfied. This prevents oscillation between states under sustained overload.

**P3.2.F5 (Recovery design):** Recovery phase uses gradual ramp-up: on entry set admit_budget = shedding_rate, each T_ramp_tick increase by delta. If ANY overload signal fires during recovery, immediately transition back to Shedding. This is the AIMD multiplicative decrease applied at the FSM level.

**P3.2.F6 (Composition):** Overload FSM operates at per-coordinator level, NOT per-shard. Acts as pre-admission filter — rejects requests before they touch ShardRecord. Cannot violate any ShardRecord invariant (INV-1 through INV-10). Composes orthogonally with ShardStatus FSM.

### Adversarial Concerns

**P4.1.F1 (Devil's Advocate):** The FSM uses count-based signals (active_lease_ratio = active_leases / total_shards), NOT wall-clock measurements. This respects sans-IO determinism. The signal is computed from coordinator state (shard map iteration), not external input.

**P1.3.F6 (Goodput collapse):** The 4-state model prevents the admit-all/reject-all oscillation. Hysteresis gaps (enter at 0.85, exit at 0.60) ensure the system doesn't flap between states.

## Proposed Types

### OverloadState enum

New file: crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/overload.rs

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
#[repr(u8)]
pub enum OverloadState {
    Normal = 0,
    Recovering = 1,
    Degraded = 2,
    Shedding = 3,
}

- repr(u8) discriminant encodes restriction ordering (matches ShardStatus pattern in record.rs)
- PartialOrd/Ord derived — enables monotonic ordering comparison

### OverloadController struct

pub struct OverloadController {
    state: OverloadState,
    entered_at: LogicalTime,
    /// Fixed-point PPM (0..=1_000_000) for deterministic simulation.
    admit_budget_ppm: u32,
    /// Sliding window of lease pressure samples.
    lease_pressure: RingBuffer<u32, 16>,
    /// Configuration thresholds
    config: OverloadConfig,
}

pub struct OverloadConfig {
    /// Enter Degraded when active_lease_ratio exceeds this (PPM)
    degrade_threshold_ppm: u32,  // default: 850_000 (85%)
    /// Enter Shedding when active_lease_ratio exceeds this (PPM)
    shed_threshold_ppm: u32,     // default: 950_000 (95%)
    /// Exit Shedding -> Recovering when below this (PPM)
    recover_threshold_ppm: u32,  // default: 700_000 (70%)
    /// Exit Recovering -> Normal when below this (PPM)
    normal_threshold_ppm: u32,   // default: 600_000 (60%)
    /// Ticks a threshold must be sustained before transition
    sustain_ticks: u64,          // default: 5
    /// AIMD additive increase per recovery tick (PPM)
    recovery_delta_ppm: u32,     // default: 50_000 (5%)
}

### Transition Diagram

                    sustained pressure > 85%
    Normal ────────────────────────────────> Degraded
      ^                                        |
      |  cooldown + budget >= 100%             | pressure > 95%
      |                                        v
    Recovering <──────────────────────── Shedding
      |              pressure < 70%            ^
      |                                        |
      +──── overload signal during recovery ───+
           (multiplicative: reset budget to shedding floor)

### Illegal Transitions

- Normal -> Shedding (must pass through Degraded)
- Normal -> Recovering (recovery only from restriction)
- Degraded -> Normal (must go through Recovering)
- Shedding -> Normal or Shedding -> Degraded (must go through Recovering)

## Files to Modify

1. **New: crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/overload.rs**
   - OverloadState enum
   - OverloadConfig struct
   - OverloadController struct with methods:
     - pub fn new(config: OverloadConfig) -> Self
     - pub fn state(&self) -> OverloadState

## Finding: Token cross-check block is dead code

**Severity**: CONSIDER
**File(s)**: crates/gossip-connectors/src/in_memory.rs:244-251
**Type**: bug (dead code)

### Problem

In enumerate_page_bounds, the token cross-check block (lines 244-251) can never change start_idx. After start_idx = start_idx.max(expected) on line 238, start_idx >= expected. The if-guard requires token_idx == expected, so start_idx.max(token_idx) == start_idx.max(expected) == start_idx. The assignment is a no-op.

The block compiles and runs correctly because the key-based path handles everything, but the code is misleading — it looks like it does something when it doesn't. The module docs claim tokens serve as a 'consistency cross-check' but no observable check occurs.

Convert the dead assignment into a debug_assert_eq! that actually validates token/key consistency. For this deterministic in-memory connector, tokens are self-produced and data is immutable, so a mismatch would indicate a connector bug. The debug_assert fires in test/debug builds but is stripped in release, preserving the 'advisory' contract.

- [ ] Dead start_idx assignment removed

title: Eliminate post-startup allocations in coordination error paths
description:
## Context
Error paths still allocate by cloning keys/spec boundaries and boxing error details. Even though lower frequency, these allocations can occur post-startup during production fault handling, violating strict allocator-closed requirements.

## Current State
Validation and split-bound checks materialize owned bytes in error variants.

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/validation.rs:227-229
return Err(CoordError::CursorRegression {
    old_key: Some(old_key.to_vec().into_boxed_slice()),
    new_key: Some(new_last_key.to_vec().into_boxed_slice()),
});
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/validation.rs:236-241
return Err(CoordError::CursorOutOfBounds(Box::new(
    CursorOutOfBoundsDetail {
        last_key: new_last_key.to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
        spec_start: spec_start.to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
        spec_end: spec_end.to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
    },
)));
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/shard_spec.rs:1194-1205
return Err(SplitValidationError::StartMismatch {
    parent_start: parent_start.to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
    first_child_start: indexed[0].1.key_range_start().to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
});
...
return Err(SplitValidationError::EndMismatch {
    parent_end: parent_end.to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
    last_child_end: last.1.key_range_end().to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
});
```

## Desired State
Runtime error reporting in production no-allocation mode uses borrowed/fixed-size diagnostics (or redacted compact codes) without heap allocation after startup, while keeping rich owned errors available for tests/dev tooling where needed.

## Implementation Guidance
### Files to Modify
| File | Change | Rationale |
|------|--------|-----------|
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/validation.rs | Introduce no-allocation error detail path (borrowed/scratch or compact enum) | Remove error-path allocations |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/shard_spec.rs | Refactor split validation errors to avoid per-error byte cloning in production mode | Keep validation allocation-stable |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs | Remove/replace split error boxing allocations where applicable | Complete split error-path cleanup |
| crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/error.rs | Separate rich owned diagnostics from runtime no-alloc diagnostics if needed | Preserve observability/debuggability |

### Patterns to Follow
Consider dual-mode error strategy:
1. allocation-free runtime error codes + bounded metadata,
2. optional rich owned expansion behind test/dev features.

### Utilities to Reuse
- Existing size limits (`MAX_KEY_SIZE`) for bounded diagnostic buffers
- Existing typed error enums to avoid ad-hoc string formatting allocations

### Blast Radius
- checkpoint/complete validation failures
- split precondition validation failures
- call sites matching detailed error fields in tests

## Code References
```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/shard_spec.rs:1219-1224
child_end: indexed[i].1.key_range_end().to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
next_child_start: indexed[i + 1]
    .1
    .key_range_start()
    .to_vec()
    .into_boxed_slice(),
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/shard_spec.rs:1332-1340
return Err(SplitValidationError::StartMismatch {
    parent_start: old_parent_start.to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
    first_child_start: new_parent.key_range_start().to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
});
...
parent_end: old_parent_end.to_vec().into_boxed_slice(),
```

```rust
// crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:1452-1454
return Err(SplitReplaceError::SplitInvalid(Box::new(
    SplitValidationError::InvalidChildSpec { child_index: i },
)));
```

## Risk Analysis
Error payload changes can affect debugging ergonomics and tests that assert rich fields. Plan migration carefully with compatibility adapters or feature-gated detailed diagnostics.

## Testing Strategy
- Add tests verifying runtime no-allocation error path behavior for common failure modes.
- Keep existing semantic assertions for error classification and tenant isolation.

## Related Work
| Task ID | Title | Relationship |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| gossip-gvft | Remove split operation temporary Vec/HashSet allocations | relates-to |
| gossip-oi59 | Tier-2: Remove acquire/snapshot allocations after startup | relates-to |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Production runtime error paths avoid heap allocation after startup warmup.
- [ ] Error classification and API contracts remain stable.
- [ ] Tests cover representative validation/split failure scenarios in no-allocation mode.
- [ ] All existing tests pass: `cargo test`.
- [ ] Code compiles clean: `cargo fmt --all && cargo check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
- [ ] Docs build clean: `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`.

## Pointers
- Audit anchors: `validation.rs:227-240`, `shard_spec.rs:1187-1230`, `1323-1340`, `in_memory.rs:1452`.
- Define clear policy for rich diagnostics versus strict no-allocation runtime mode.

Add per-worker claim cooldown to prevent coordinator saturation
description:
## Overview

Add per-worker claim cooldown to prevent tight-loop claim_next_available calls that create O(N*S) coordinator work. This is the critical unmitigated overload vector identified by adversarial review.

## Research Evidence

### Why Claim Cooldown Is Critical

**P4.2.F8 (Cross-Validator):** 'Pull-based workers cannot push load onto the coordinator' is OVERSTATED. claim_next_available in facade.rs does O(S) scan + up to O(S) acquire attempts per call. A burst of N workers calling claim simultaneously generates O(N*S) work on the single &mut self coordinator. Claiming IS load.

**P4.3.F13 (Assumptions Auditor):** Nothing throttles a worker calling claim_next_available in a tight loop. A single runaway worker can monopolize the coordinator's &mut self lock, starving all others of checkpoint/renew calls.

**P4.3.F1 (Assumptions Auditor):** claim_next_available in facade.rs:193-223 does O(S) scan + up to O(S) acquire attempts per call. Hot-loop claim storms saturate coordinator; starvation of checkpoint/renew calls that share the same &mut self lock.

**P1.3.F1 (Metastable failures, Bronson et al. OSDI 2021):** Pull-based workers that fail-and-re-poll create amplification loops. A burst of lease expirations triggers mass re-acquisition, deepening overload. The lease-expiry thundering herd (P1.3.F5, Chubby OSDI 2006) is the concrete manifestation.

**P1.3.F5 (Lease expiry thundering herd):** When overload causes lease holders to miss renewal deadlines, all leases expire simultaneously. Subsequent re-acquisition storm creates thundering herd. Without jitter (P4.3.F6 confirmed zero hits for 'jitter' in codebase), this is unmitigated.

### Relationship to Credit Piggybacking (gossip-tybv)

This issue complements the credit piggybacking issue. Credit signals (available_count, earliest_expiry) provide the SMART retry hint — workers know WHEN to retry. Claim cooldown is the HARD FLOOR — even if a worker ignores the hint, it cannot overwhelm the coordinator. Together they form a two-layer defense:

Layer 1 (soft): earliest_expiry tells worker 'don't bother until time T'
Layer 2 (hard): claim cooldown rejects attempts within N ticks regardless

**P4.4.F4 (Contrarian):** Without any form of request halting, a coordinator failure could trigger unbounded retry storms from all session workers simultaneously. Marc Brooker's analysis shows per-client retry budgets are the minimum viable protection.

## Files to Modify

1. **crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/facade.rs:80-90** — Add variant to ClaimError:
   - Throttled { retry_after: LogicalTime } — worker must wait until retry_after before next claim attempt
   - Update ClaimError Display impl
   - Update compile-time size guard (line 123: assert size <= 48)

2. **crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/facade.rs:175-236** — Modify default_claim_next_available:
   - Option A (preferred): Add min_claim_interval parameter and last_claim_times tracker
   - Option B: Create claim_with_cooldown wrapper that calls existing default_claim_next_available
   - Before scanning candidates, check last_claim_times.get(worker). If within cooldown, return Err(ClaimError::Throttled { retry_after: last + min_claim_interval })
   - On successful acquire, update last_claim_times.insert(worker, now)

3. **crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:134-155** — Add to InMemoryCoordinator:
   - claim_cooldowns: BTreeMap<WorkerId, LogicalTime> — tracks last successful claim per worker
   - min_claim_interval: u64 — configurable cooldown duration (same pattern as default_lease_duration)
   - Add to constructor (new/with_limits or a new with_cooldown builder method)

4. **crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs** — In the ShardClaiming impl:
   - The blanket impl of ShardClaiming delegates to default_claim_next_available (facade.rs:273-286)
   - The cooldown check should go HERE (at the impl level) since InMemoryCoordinator owns the cooldown state
   - Override claim_next_available on InMemoryCoordinator directly (the blanket impl has a default body)
   - OR add the cooldown as a pre-check in a wrapper method

5. **crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory_tests.rs** — New tests:
   - rapid_claim_throttled: two claims from same worker in quick succession, second returns Throttled
   - different_workers_not_throttled: two different workers can claim simultaneously
   - claim_after_cooldown_succeeds: advance time past cooldown, claim succeeds
   - throttled_retry_after_is_correct: verify retry_after = last_claim_time + min_claim_interval
   - cooldown_does_not_affect_renew_or_checkpoint: verify cooldown only gates claiming, not other ops

## Design Decisions

1. **Per-worker, not per-(worker, run):** Initially simpler. A worker throttled on run A is also throttled on run B. This prevents a worker from flooding claims across multiple runs. Can be refined to per-(worker, run) later if needed.

2. **Cooldown on successful claim only:** Failed claims (NoneAvailable) do NOT trigger cooldown. This prevents a worker from being punished for asking when nothing is available. Only successful acquisition triggers the cooldown window.

3. **BTreeMap not HashMap:** Consistent with InvariantChecker pattern (invariants.rs:84-86). BTreeMap<WorkerId, LogicalTime> provides deterministic iteration order for simulation reproducibility.

4. **Configurable interval:** Like default_lease_duration (in_memory.rs:152), min_claim_interval is an operational parameter. Default: 1 tick (prevents tight-loop but doesn't add artificial delay). Production tuning via with_limits or builder.

5. **retry_after in error:** The Throttled error carries the exact time to retry (deterministic, LogicalTime-based). This is the claim cooldown equivalent of earliest_expiry from the credit piggybacking issue. Workers get deterministic retry guidance, not jitter.

6. **Does NOT modify CoordinationBackend trait:** Cooldown is an orchestration concern, not a protocol concern. It lives in the facade/impl layer, not the core trait. acquire_and_restore remains cooldown-unaware.

## Risk Mitigations

- **Starvation prevention:** Cooldown is per-worker. One worker's cooldown doesn't block others. Combined with the existing deterministic offset in claim_next_available (worker.as_raw() % len at facade.rs:191), workers spread across candidates.
- **Metastable failure prevention (P1.3.F1):** Cooldown breaks the feedback loop: overload -> lease expiry -> re-acquisition storm -> deeper overload. Workers that lost leases must wait min_claim_interval before re-polling.
- **No goodput impact (P1.3.F6):** Cooldown only gates NEW claims. Active sessions (checkpoint, renew, complete, park, split) are unaffected. Workers already holding leases continue processing at full speed.

## References

1. Bronson et al., 'Metastable Failures in Distributed Systems,' OSDI 2021 — sustaining feedback loops
2. Burrows, 'The Chubby Lock Service,' OSDI 2006 — lease expiry thundering herd
3. Marc Brooker, 'Fixing retries,' 2022 — per-client retry budgets as minimum protection
4. Google SRE Book Ch. 21 — retry budgets (max 3 retries/request, 10% ratio/client)
5. Amazon Builders' Library — break positive feedback loops, shed early/cheap

Document logical_time overflow risk in LWW timestamp encoding
description:
## Context
The persistence doc (docs/boundary-5-persistence.md Section 3.3) defines LWW timestamp encoding as:
```
USING TIMESTAMP = (status_discriminant << 56) | logical_time
```
If logical_time exceeds 2^56-1 (72,057,594,037,927,935), it will bleed into the status discriminant bits, corrupting the CRDT merge semantics. The doc does not specify the valid range or type of logical_time.

## Current State
docs/boundary-5-persistence.md lines 210-217 define the encoding but do not constrain the logical_time range.

## Desired State
Add a constraint note specifying:
- logical_time MUST be < 2^56 (72 quadrillion)
- If using nanosecond timestamps from epoch, this overflows circa year 2242 — document that this is safe
- If using a logical clock, document the reset/wrap behavior
- Consider adding a runtime assertion in the production implementation

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Section 3.3 documents the valid range of logical_time
- [ ] Overflow scenario and safety margin are explicitly stated
close_reason: Already documented: Section 3.3 lines 214-219 of boundary-5-persistence.md document the 56-bit constraint, microsecond overflow horizon (~2.28 billion years), and mandate to reject/mask values >= 2^56.

## Finding: Huge slices wrap when downcasted, causing undersized reservation

**Severity**: MUST FIX
**File(s)**: crates/gossip-stdx/src/byte_slab.rs:67-305
**Type**: safety

### Problem
`alloc_size` casts `usize` lengths to `u32` without bounds checking. For lengths greater than `u32::MAX`, the cast wraps and the allocator may reserve fewer bytes than intended before copying `data.len()` bytes, leading to panic and a denial-of-service vector.

### Resolution Steps
1. Add an edge-case test that verifies oversized logical lengths are rejected by the allocator's sizing/validation path.
2. Implement explicit length validation so inputs that do not fit in `u32` are rejected before allocation/copy.
3. Ensure bounds checks and invariants are documented inline where needed.
4. Run tests and quality gates.

title: Tier-2: Remove acquire/snapshot allocations after startup
description:
## Context
Tier-1 (borrowed `CursorUpdate` for checkpoint/complete) has been implemented and validated, removing owned-cursor heap churn from steady-state mutation paths. The remaining allocation hotspot is Tier-2: acquire/snapshot materialization still allocates owned `ShardSpec`/`Cursor` payloads on every acquire, which prevents a strict post-startup no-allocation runtime.

This follow-up task tracks eliminating those acquire-path allocations using existing slab-backed/borrowed patterns (no new allocator design).

## Current State
`acquire_and_restore` still returns an owned `ShardSnapshot`, and snapshot creation materializes owned structures from pooled slab fields.

- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs:980-989`
  - `record.snapshot(&self.slab)` is called inside acquire and returned in `AcquireResult`.
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/record.rs:711-721`
  - `snapshot()` builds `ShardSnapshot::new(... self.spec.to_spec(slab), self.cursor.to_cursor(slab), ...)`.
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/pooled.rs:189-195`
  - `PooledShardSpec::to_spec()` allocates owned bytes (`.into()` on slices).
- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/pooled.rs:334-348`
  - `PooledCursor::to_cursor()` allocates owned bytes (`to_vec()` and owned `Cursor`).

## Desired State
Introduce an acquire-path API that avoids per-acquire heap materialization by borrowing from slab-backed state or by using reusable caller-provided scratch buffers. The steady-state acquire/checkpoint/complete lifecycle should be allocation-free after startup warmup.

## Implementation Guidance
- Reuse existing tested patterns already present in this repo and companion systems (borrowed views + reusable scratch), instead of introducing a new allocator abstraction.
- Prefer staged migration:
  1. Add borrowed snapshot/spec/cursor view types for runtime paths.
  2. Keep owned snapshot APIs for compatibility where needed.
  3. Move hot call paths to borrowed APIs first.
- Preserve existing invariants and idempotency/hash behavior.
- Ensure no slab slot aliasing or lifetime unsoundness is introduced.

- `crates/gossip-contracts/src/coordination/in_memory.rs`

Multi-tenant simulation scenario
description:
## Multi-tenant simulation scenario

### Problem
All simulation runs use a single hardcoded TenantId ([0x01; 32]) at harness.rs:627. The InMemoryCoordinator uses a two-level HashMap<TenantId, HashMap<ShardKey, ShardRecord>> which structurally isolates tenants. The RejectionKind::TenantMismatch variant (harness.rs:235) exists with From impls for all error types (lines 259, 272, 287, 303, 317, 331) but is DEAD CODE in simulation — it can never fire because only one tenant exists. The InvariantChecker already keys history by TenantId (type HistoryKey = (TenantId, RunId, ShardId) at invariants.rs:179) and has a dedicated unit test cross_tenant_isolation_in_temporal_checks (invariants.rs:1112) — but this tests the CHECKER, not the coordinator under fault injection.

### Research Basis

**P1.1.F6 (Non-Interference Property, Evidence 4):** Multi-tenant isolation formally maps to non-interference (Goguen & Meseguer 1982): operations by tenant A produce no observable effect on tenant B's state. The coordinator enforces this via TenantMismatch errors at every entry point. Simulation should verify non-interference, not just structural enforcement.

**P1.4.F7 (Multi-Tenant via Parameterized Configs, Evidence 3):** Two approaches: (A) rstest parameterization for fixed tenant configs, (B) proptest strategy for (n_tenants, shard_distribution). The simplest path is a standalone deterministic test exercising InMemoryCoordinator directly with two tenants.

**P1.5.F4 (Multi-Tenant Isolation Testing Gap, Evidence 5):** The InvariantChecker's tenant-scoped history paths and check_all method's tenant filter are never exercised with multiple tenants in simulation. Jepsen consistently finds isolation violations among the most common distributed system bugs.

**Turso Incident (2023-12-04):** A migration bug created databases with empty backup identifiers, causing multiple databases to share backup storage. Multi-tenancy tests confirming data cannot cross-contaminate would have caught this. Source: turso.tech/blog/incident-2023-12-04-data-leak-and-loss-in-some-free-tier-databases-7cba5bc7

### Files to Modify
- crates/gossip-contracts/src/sim/mega_sim_tests.rs (add standalone test)

### Implementation (Standalone test, no harness changes)

Add a multi_tenant_isolation test directly in mega_sim_tests.rs:

1. Setup:
   - Create InMemoryCoordinator::new(DEFAULT_LEASE_DURATION)
   - Create InvariantChecker::new()
   - Define tenant_a = TenantId::from_bytes([0x01; 32])
   - Define tenant_b = TenantId::from_bytes([0x02; 32])
   - Register run_a (RunId::from_raw(1)) with 3 shards for tenant_a using seed_shard + seed_run
   - Register run_b (RunId::from_raw(2)) with 3 shards for tenant_b using seed_shard + seed_run

2. Phase A — Normal lifecycle for tenant A:
   - acquire_and_restore(now, tenant_a, key_a1, worker_1) — expect Ok
   - checkpoint(now, tenant_a, &lease_a, cursor, op_id) — expect Ok
   - complete(now, tenant_a, &lease_a, cursor, op_id) — expect Ok
   - After each: checker.check_all(&coordinator, tenant_a, now)

3. Phase B — Cross-tenant isolation:
   - acquire_and_restore(now, tenant_b, key_a1, worker_2) — expect ShardNotFound
     (tenant B cannot see tenant A's shards)
   - Create a fake lease for tenant_b but with tenant_a's shard key — attempt
     checkpoint — expect TenantMismatch or ShardNotFound
   - After each: checker.check_all for BOTH tenants

4. Phase C — Independent lifecycle for tenant B:
   - acquire_and_restore(now, tenant_b, key_b1, worker_2) — expect Ok
   - checkpoint and complete on tenant B's shards
   - After each: checker.check_all for BOTH tenants
   - Verify tenant A's records are unchanged

5. Assertions:
   - Zero invariant violations across all operations for both tenants
   - Cross-tenant operations correctly rejected (ShardNotFound, not panic)
   - Each tenant's shard records are independently correct
   - TenantMismatch code path exercised at least once

### Key Code References
- harness.rs:627 — single tenant: TenantId::from_bytes([0x01; 32])
- harness.rs:235 — RejectionKind::TenantMismatch (dead code in current sim)
- harness.rs:259,272,287,303,317,331 — From impls mapping TenantMismatch errors
- invariants.rs:179 — HistoryKey = (TenantId, RunId, ShardId) (already tenant-scoped)
